analysis.title: USA: Core Capital Goods Orders in Line With Expectations but Shipments Above Expectations; Boosting Q3 GDP Tracking Estimate to 3.4%
key_insights: New orders for durable goods rose 1.8% MoM in September, roughly in line with the median forecast of +1.9%. The increase largely reflects commercial aircraft orders.

Durable goods ex-transportation rose 0.5% MoM against a median forecast of +0.6%, and core capital goods orders rose 0.5% against a median of +0.7%. The gains were driven by new orders for computers and related products and machinery.
Core capital goods shipments rose 1.2% MoM, above the median forecast of +0.8% and GS +1.0%. Manufacturing inventories rose 0.4%.
August was revised up for durable goods orders (+0.2pp to +0.1%), durable goods ex-transportation (+0.1pp to +0.3%) and core capital goods shipments (+0.1pp to +0.6%).

Core capital goods shipments and the inventory details were slightly stronger than GS's previous GDP tracking assumptions. GS raised its Q3 GDP tracking estimate by 0.1pp to +3.4% quarter-over-quarter annualized.
